detail: Addressing the Thursday morning plenary of the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, Xi Jinping set out a programme built on four pillars - economy and trade, connectivity, innovation and development - and announced that China will provide $20 million to support APEC's practical cooperation. He also announced a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen for policy research and exchanges, and new cooperation institutions covering digital technology, cross-border data flows, clean energy and small and medium-sized enterprise development. On trade, he presented the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific (FTAAP) as a shared vision of APEC members and called for steady progress toward it, with aligned regional trade agreements and deeper policy dialogue.
fact: China pledges $20m; new Asia-Pacific research centre
headline: Xi pledges $20 million and a Shenzhen research centre at APEC plenary
summary: Xi used his APEC plenary address to pledge $20m for APEC cooperation and unveil a Shenzhen research centre and new bodies on data, clean energy and small firms.

detail: As of mid-afternoon Thursday (~15:45 WIB), no Shenzhen Declaration text had been issued. Asia Today's closing-day report, published 12:23 WIB and read in full, still carried the declaration under 'still to come': leaders were expected to adopt it before the meeting closed on Thursday, with Putin having confirmed Moscow's support for the draft text. Adoption needs consensus of all 21 member economies. Per Deputy Foreign Minister Ma Zhaoxu (round 1), the draft sets out a roadmap toward an Asia-Pacific community on trade, connectivity, innovation and development, with a standalone FTAAP statement and an AI cooperation document also prepared. PENDING: record as still pending, not adopted, until an issued text is reported by a named outlet.
fact: no declaration text issued by ~15:45 WIB
headline: Shenzhen Declaration still not issued as APEC leaders' meeting closes
summary: The Shenzhen Declaration had not been issued by mid-afternoon Thursday; leaders were expected to adopt it before the close, and Putin backed the draft.

detail: The first trilateral meeting of Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin took place in Shenzhen on Thursday, alongside a separate Trump-Putin bilateral of about 40 minutes which the Kremlin said focused primarily on Ukraine. The Wall Street Journal reported Trump framed his 'very special relationship' with Xi as the cornerstone of US-China stability, while US officials played down prospects of a breakthrough. The agenda covered nuclear arms control - the New START treaty expired in February 2026 - the Ukraine and Iran wars, trade and AI. No joint statement had been announced and no agreements were reported by collection time; officials described the meetings as an opening for further talks rather than deal-making (Particle News).
fact: first trilateral held; no agreements announced
headline: Xi, Trump and Putin hold first trilateral with no agreements announced
summary: The first Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral met in Shenzhen on Thursday; a 40-minute Trump-Putin talk focused on Ukraine, and no agreements were announced.

detail: More than 30 European leaders gathered in Berlin on Thursday for a Coalition of the Willing summit hosted by Chancellor Friedrich Merz with France's Emmanuel Macron and Britain's Andy Burnham, attended by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. The meeting aims to lock in long-term military and financial support for Kyiv and secure a European seat in any peace negotiations - Moscow has not agreed to European participation. On Wednesday the European Commission proposed an additional €45 billion loan for Ukraine in 2027 (up to €25bn military aid, €20bn budget support), still leaving a projected €25bn gap against a €70bn need. Germany and Norway each announced $300 million for NATO's PURL programme, and Britain announced a £260 million package including more than 1,000 long-range strike drones (Reuters).
fact: EC proposed €45bn loan for Ukraine in 2027
headline: Europe's Coalition of the Willing meets in Berlin to fund Ukraine
summary: More than 30 European leaders met in Berlin to lock in Ukraine funding and demand a European seat in peace talks, as Trump's envoys attended.

detail: COP31 entered its final stretch on Thursday with ministers sharply divided over the pace of a fossil fuel phaseout, and no agreed cover text yet ahead of the Friday, Nov 20 close. Presidency figures Murat Kurum and Chris Bowen convened informal minister-level talks in Turkey's Divan format, urging delegations to find common ground rather than restate positions. The IEA released its World Energy Outlook on Thursday; executive director Fatih Birol said the Hormuz crisis 'has delivered a huge shock to the system' and saw no credible pathway for energy markets to return to how they were before. The second Global Stocktake, launched on Wednesday, still had 21 issues unresolved, with new draft texts due; Saudi Arabia, Russia and Gulf states are pushing back against explicit fossil fuel references (Nation Press, read in full).
headline: COP31 enters final stretch split on fossil fuels as Divan talks open
summary: COP31's final stretch opened with ministers split over fossil-fuel phaseout pace; the presidency turned to Divan talks and the IEA warned Hormuz has reshaped energy.

detail: Odisha's evacuation has climbed steeply past the morning figure: a Revenue and Disaster Management Department official said more than 80,000 people had been shifted to safety against the state's 2 lakh (204,070) target, superseding the 46,701 moved reported earlier on Thursday. Ganjam district alone had shifted 36,398 people by 6 am Thursday, with 308 shelters operational and 1,098 pregnant women moved to safety; 74 rescue teams are deployed across 11 districts, and railways cancelled two Visakhapatnam-Koraput trains for Thursday and Friday. The IMD morning bulletin is unchanged: Akvan crosses between Narsapur and Puri, close to east of Gopalpur, by Friday noon with winds of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110, and a 0.5-1 metre storm surge is likely in Ganjam and Puri (The Hindu BusinessLine, read in full).
headline: Odisha evacuation passes 80,000 as Cyclone Akvan nears landfall
summary: Odisha has now moved more than 80,000 people to safety ahead of Cyclone Akvan, superseding the 46,701 morning figure, with landfall due Friday noon near Gopalpur.

detail: Thursday's new framing for the round-1 Gaza story: the Israeli tank incursion beyond the Yellow Line - the first since the October 2025 ceasefire - coincided with a visit to Israel by the chief of US Central Command, who met the IDF chief of staff and the Mossad director for talks focused on regional security challenges and the escalation with Iran. An AFP journalist observed tanks positioned east of the Nuseirat refugee camp; the IDF and Shin Bet said the operation was dismantling a tunnel west of the Yellow Line that posed an immediate threat to Israeli forces, part of the Salah a-Din road was closed, and hundreds of Palestinians fled their shelters. DATE NOTE: the incursion itself began on Wednesday, Nov 18; it is not a new Thursday event (NationScope News, read in full).
fact: CENTCOM chief in Israel as tanks crossed the line
headline: Gaza ground operation coincides with visit of US CENTCOM chief
summary: Israel's first tank incursion beyond the Yellow Line since the ceasefire coincided with the CENTCOM chief's visit to Israel for talks on Iran and regional security.

detail: Russia's transport ministry has now characterised the overnight third attack on the Crimean Bridge as a nighttime drone attack that led to the temporary suspension of train services on the railway section; officials said nobody was injured and specialists were assessing the damage. Crimea's Russian-installed head Sergei Aksyonov confirmed the bridge had been attacked and traffic halted. The extent of any new structural damage remained undisclosed at collection time, and Ukraine has not commented on the latest attack. This adds the official Russian characterisation to round 1's Guardian account; it does not change the underlying event, which took place overnight into Thursday.
fact: transport ministry: drone attack, no injuries
headline: Russia says drone attack halted Kerch rail traffic; no injuries
summary: Russia's transport ministry said a nighttime drone attack suspended Kerch Bridge rail services with no injuries, as crews assessed damage from the third strike.

detail: Pre-open analyst framing ahead of ANT's Nasdaq debut at 09:30 ET (21:30 WIB) today: New Street Research initiated with a buy rating and a $105 target, with analyst Pierre Ferragu calling Anthropic a 'generational IPO' (CNBC, via Fast Company, read in full); Morningstar set a $92 fair value and sees the stock as undervalued. The lead underwriters Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are in a research quiet period, leaving independent houses to set the tone. Caution flags: Morningstar criticised a governance structure in which founders control 50.1% of votes, and Orbis's Ben Preston said his fund would not buy at this valuation; the S-1 shows nine-month 2026 revenue of $33.2 billion, up more than 1,200% year over year, alongside a $104 billion net loss. The debut is being framed as a test of investor appetite for AI after a sector pullback. NO PRICE ACTION EXISTS YET: the first trade prints after the 21:30 WIB open.
headline: Analysts call Anthropic a 'generational IPO' ahead of Nasdaq open
summary: Ahead of ANT's 21:30 WIB Nasdaq open, New Street calls Anthropic a 'generational IPO' with a $105 target and Morningstar sees $92 fair value; sceptics cite valuation.

detail: Parts of Bangladesh shut down on Thursday as the Awami League's nationwide lockdown capped a week-long campaign against the government's refusal to issue Sheikh Hasina a new passport and identity card for her planned December return from exile in India. Police said two ruling party members were killed, and 97 Border Guard platoons fanned out across seven districts. Authorities on Thursday detained former education minister Nurul Islam Nahid over killings during the 2024 protests. At least 37 Grameen Bank branches have been targeted in arson attacks since Nov 10, and police report crude bomb blasts and vehicle fires in at least 28 districts over the last 10 days. DATE NOTE: the ancestral home of former interim leader Muhammad Yunus, in Chattogram, was set on fire late on Wednesday, Nov 18; his family members in the house are safe (Reuters, read in full).
fact: two killed; 97 Border Guard platoons deployed
headline: Bangladesh lockdown turns violent as Yunus family home is torched
summary: An Awami League lockdown shut parts of Bangladesh on Thursday; police said two ruling party members were killed and Muhammad Yunus's ancestral home was set ablaze.

detail: Fiji has declared a national state of disaster for one month over an El Niño-driven drought causing widespread water shortages, setting aside 20 million Fiji dollars ($8.5 million), redeployed from existing funds, for emergency water supplies for families and farmers; more than two million litres of emergency water were delivered to maritime communities over the preceding month. DATE LABEL: Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka announced the declaration in a national address on Wednesday, Nov 18; Reuters reported it on Thursday, Nov 19. The Fiji Meteorological Service forecasts below-normal rainfall from November through at least April, and the US Climate Prediction Center puts the chance of a strong-to-very-strong El Niño through January-March above 79% (Reuters).
fact: FJ$20m response; rain below normal until April
headline: Fiji declares national disaster over El Niño drought
summary: Fiji declared a one-month national state of disaster over an El Niño drought, setting aside FJ$20m as its weather bureau forecasts below-normal rain until April.
